title: finding(types): `BaseSchema.testId`'s JSDoc promises "Rendered as data-testid attribute" — nothing renders it, and it reaches the DOM as a lowercase `testid`
body:
Found while fixing objectui#8234 (the `scroll-area.mdx` schema fence). Measured on `origin/main` `0fa7a9c83`. Exact class-mirror of objectui#7088 (`BaseSchema.hidden`'s JSDoc promising `visibility: hidden` while the renderer returns null) — same interface, different key, and that one is closed.

## The claim

`packages/types/src/base.ts:419-423`:

```ts
  /**
   * Test ID for automated testing.
   * Rendered as data-testid attribute.
   */
  testId?: string;
```

## What actually happens

**1. Nothing in the repo reads `schema.testId`.** `git grep 'schema\.testId' packages/` returns exactly two hits, and neither is a read into the DOM:

- `packages/core/src/builder/schema-builder.ts:84` — `this.schema.testId = testId;`, which *writes* it;
- `packages/core/src/builder/__tests__/schema-builder.test.ts:177` — the assertion that the write happened.

The ~40 other `testId` hits across `packages/*/src` are ordinary React component props on hand-written components (`PageHeader`, `HomeRail`, the metadata-admin inspectors, …), unrelated to the schema key.

**2. `SchemaRenderer` does not strip it, so it is spread as a raw React prop.** The metadata destructure at `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx:1451-1478` names `type` / `children` / `body` / `visible` / `visibleWhen` / `visibleOn` / `visibility` / `hidden` / `hiddenOn` / `disabled` / `disabledOn` / `dataSource` / `responsiveStyles` and the two internal flags. `testId` is not in that list, so it lands in `componentProps` and is spread onto the component, which spreads it onto the DOM element.

**3. React writes it as `testid`, not `data-testid`.** Measured through `SchemaRenderer` with a `ui:scroll-area` node (`testId: 'my-tid'`):

```
[data-testid="my-tid"] present = false
[testid="my-tid"]      present = true
outerHTML head = DIV dir="ltr" class="relative overflow-hidden" style="…" testid="my-tid" data-obj-type="scroll-area"
                 (opening tag; angle brackets written out as DIV so this body survives the sanitizer)
```

So the attribute an author gets is `testid`, a non-standard attribute that no test-library query helper looks for. `screen.getByTestId(…)` and `[data-testid=…]` both miss it. A contrast leg in the same run: `id: 'my-scroll'` **does** reach the DOM correctly, as `id="my-scroll"` plus `data-obj-id="my-scroll"` — so the strip list and the spread are working as designed; it is only this key that has no mapping.

## Why it matters beyond one key

The row is published to authors. `testId?: string;` appears in the "Base properties" block of **16 component doc pages** (`grep -rlF '// Base properties' content/docs/components/` — `basic/div`, `basic/span`, `complex/carousel`, `complex/data-table`, `complex/filter-builder`, `complex/resizable`, `complex/scroll-area`, `data-display/statistic`, `data-display/tree-view`, `feedback/toaster`, `form/calendar`, `form/file-upload`, `layout/box`, `layout/page`, `layout/semantic`, `navigation/header-bar`). An author who reads any of them, writes `testId: 'x'`, and then writes `getByTestId('x')` gets a failing test with no diagnostic pointing anywhere near the cause.

The zod twin declares it too (`packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts:229`, `testId: z.string().optional().describe('Test identifier')`), so it validates cleanly on the way in.

## Not fixed under objectui#8234

That card is the `scroll-area` reference page and its fence. The `testId` row on that page is **accurate against the declaration**, so correcting the page would have meant making it disagree with `base.ts` to route around a defect elsewhere — the lenient-fallback shape AGENTS.md #0.1 forbids. Left alone there deliberately, and filed here instead. Contract-first, the fix is at the producer, and it is one of two directions:

- **A — make the promise true.** Add `testId` to `SchemaRenderer`'s metadata destructure and emit `data-testid={schema.testId}` alongside the existing `data-obj-id` / `data-obj-type`. Every one of the 16 doc pages then becomes correct with no doc edit. Risk: it adds an attribute to rendered output, so any snapshot holding a node that authors `testId` moves.
- **B — retire the promise.** Delete the "Rendered as data-testid attribute" sentence, or the key, under the enforce-or-remove reading: it has one writer, no reader, and its only observable effect today is a stray non-standard DOM attribute. Needs the 16 doc pages updated if the key goes.

Not choosing between them here — that is a contract decision. Note that objectui#7088 (the same shape on `hidden`) resolved by making the *declaration* honest rather than by changing the renderer, which is a precedent for B, but `hidden` had a working behaviour to describe and this key has none.

## Gate blindness

Nothing catches it. `check:doc-types` reads only `type` string literals from doc code blocks. `check:doc-snippets` compiles only `ts`/`tsx`/`typescript` fences, and the Base-properties blocks on all 16 pages are fenced `plaintext`. No test asserts a `data-testid` produced from a schema node. Same class as objectui#6143.
